title: The dualizing complex of a proper scheme over a field is independent of the field of definition and compatible with field extensions
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: For a proper scheme X over a field k with omega_X^bullet and omega_X as in Lemma labelled lemma-duality-proper-over-field, the lemma asserts two things: if X -> Spec(k) factors through Spec(k') -> Spec(k) then the same objects serve for the morphism X -> Spec(k'); and for a field extension K/k the pullbacks of omega_X^bullet and omega_X to X_K serve for X_K -> Spec(K) (statement lines 7162-7205). The proof writes f for the structure morphism, f' for the factored one and recalls that in the previous lemma omega_X^bullet was defined as a(O_{Spec(k)}) for the right adjoint a of f; so it suffices to show a(O_{Spec(k)}) = a'(O_{Spec(k)}) (proof lines 7207-7219). Since k' is contained in H^0(X, O_X) the extension k'/k is finite by Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma labelled coherent-lemma-proper-over-affine-cohomology-finite; by uniqueness of adjoints a = a' o b for the right adjoint b of the morphism Spec(k') -> Spec(k), i.e. f^! = (f')^! o g^!, so it suffices to know Hom_k(k', k) = k' as k'-modules, which holds because both are one dimensional k'-vector spaces, with reference to Example labelled example-affine-twisted-inverse-image (proof lines 7221-7237). Part (2) follows from base change for a by Lemma labelled lemma-more-base-change as discussed in Remark labelled remark-relative-dualizing-complex (proof lines 7239-7240). Reducing the comparison to the finite residue field extension and then invoking base change for the adjoint is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
